content.what_it_is: This file implements FUNWAVE-TVD face-flux construction. FLUXES selects fourth-order, fourth-order/minmod, WENO, MLP, or piecewise-linear reconstruction, computes interface wave speeds, chooses HLL or centered interface fluxes, and applies boundary conditions (lines 59-126). HLL resolves left-, right-, and transonic-speed cases (lines 177-203). DelxyFun, DelxFun, and DelyFun form van-Leer-limited derivatives (lines 212-312), while WAVE_SPEED constructs gravity-wave bounds and copies interior values into ghost faces (lines 327-412). CONSTRUCTION and its HO/minmod, HO, MLP, and WENO variants reconstruct Eta, velocity, momentum, and dispersive U4/V4 states and then form PL/PR, QL/QR, and momentum fluxes (lines 425-560, 659-779, 1049-1169, 1408-1515, and 1677-1784). The directional reconstruction kernels implement piecewise-linear, minmod-limited fourth-order, hybrid van-Leer/minmod fourth-order, multidimensional limiting process, and fifth-order WENO formulas (lines 573-643, 793-1007, 1177-1401, 1520-1669, and 1791-1965).

unresolved: In CONSTRUCT_HO_X_MLP, every protective small-denominator test is executed after the corresponding division: gamL is divided at line 1546 before TXP1 is tested at line 1547; gamR at 1550 before TXP3 at 1551; tanth1/tanth2 at 1555/1559 before delsol tests at 1556/1560; and gamRtanth2/gamLtanth1 at 1562/1574 before gamma tests at 1563/1575. Zero or tiny denominators can therefore raise floating-point exceptions or create Inf/NaN before the fallback assignment, making the checks ineffective.

CONSTRUCT_HO_Y_MLP duplicates the same divide-before-check sequence: gamL/gamR at lines 1621/1625 precede denominator tests at 1622/1626; tanth1/tanth2 at 1630/1634 precede delsol tests at 1631/1635; and transverse gamma divisions at 1637/1649 precede gamma tests at 1638/1650.

The dispersive face arrays U4xL/U4xR/V4xL/V4xR and U4yL/U4yR/V4yL/V4yR are assigned only inside IF(DISPERSION) blocks (for example lines 452-460 and 511-519), but they are read unconditionally immediately afterward in PL/PR, QL/QR, and momentum-flux expressions (lines 466-555). The same copied pattern occurs in HO-minmod (lines 686-774), HO, MLP (lines 1431-1510), and WENO construction. When DISPERSION is false, this file supplies no initialization before those reads; correctness depends on external initialization and on multiplication by Gamma1 not exposing undefined values.

CONSTRUCT_HO_X_MLP and CONSTRUCT_HO_Y_MLP declare and receive MASK at lines 1526 and 1600, but their active bodies never reference MASK. Unlike the minmod/HO kernels, the MLP kernels therefore do not lower order or zero gradients at dry-neighbor stencils; the dummy-argument interface suggests wet/dry handling that is not implemented in these routines.

VANLEER_LIMITER divides by ABS(A)+ABS(B) when optional B is present and by 1.0+A otherwise (lines 1027-1030), with no local zero-denominator guard. A=B=0 and A=-1 respectively produce 0/0 if this public function is called, although active reconstruction code in this file uses inline guarded formulas instead.

The HLL transonic branch tests ABS(SR-SL)<SMALL but then divides the numerator by positive SMALL rather than by the signed speed difference (lines 193-198). This regularization changes denominator sign for a small negative SR-SL and does not establish the limiting flux; its intended behavior is unresolved.

MLP and WENO stencils access up to I-3/I+2 and J-3/J+2 while their loops are driven directly by Ibeg/Iend/Jbeg/Jend (lines 1541-1559 and 1813-1853, with y analogues). No local bounds/ghost-width assertion is present, so array safety depends on external bounds guaranteeing at least three valid ghost indices.

CONSTRUCT_X and CONSTRUCT_Y accept Kappa at lines 579 and 622, but Kappa is not used in either body; comments at lines 584-586 and 625-628 say it is meaningless. The retained interface argument can diverge from callers' expectation that Kappa selects reconstruction order.
